title: Mask the card number before a payment is logged
examObjective: Applying correct syntax to write DataWeave transformations to coerce, format, order, and filter data
basics: The `update` operator changes one field inside a value and keeps everything else as it was: `payload update { case n at .card.number -> ... }` replaces the card number and leaves the other fields alone. Inside the case, `n` is the old value.
prompt:
Payment events must be logged without the full card number. Replace `card.number` with `"**** "` followed by its last four digits, and leave every other field exactly as it was.

Card numbers are not all the same length: most are 16 digits, American Express is 15. Some events, such as bank transfers, have no `card` at all; log those unchanged.
hints: `update` changes the one field and keeps the rest. What does it do when the field is not there?
The last four characters of a String of any length: negative indexes count from the end.
`n[-4 to -1]` is the last four characters whatever the length.
solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload update { case n at .card.number -> "**** " ++ n[-4 to -1] }

mustFail.why: takes characters 12 to 15, which is the last four only for a 16-digit number
mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload update { case n at .card.number -> "**** " ++ n[12 to 15] }

mustFail.why: builds a new card object, which drops the expiry date
mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload update { case c at .card -> { number: "**** " ++ c.number[-4 to -1] } }

explanation.approach: `update` is the tool for "change one thing, keep the rest", and a case whose path is not in the data is skipped, which is exactly what the bank-transfer event needs. For the digits, fixed positions assume a fixed length; negative indexes count from the end and work for any length.

snippets.label: Fixed positions on a 15-digit number
snippets.note: Position 15 does not exist, so the whole range is null.

snippets.label: update on a missing path
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload update { case n at .card.number -> "x" }
snippets.note: Nothing to change, so nothing changes.
